blind_target.title: Job attitudes and employee engagement: Considering the "A-factor".
blind_target.evidence_quote: For the relationships among work engagement, job satisfaction, affective organizational commitment, and job involvement, we used the meta-analytic correlations from Newman et al. (2010). This allowed us to replicate and extend the work of Newman et al. by conducting new analyses on the same data.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: For example, our model produced estimated latent correlations from the A-factor of job attitudes to work engagement (φ=0.77), job satisfaction (φ=0.71), affective organizational commitment (φ=0.75), and job involvement (φ=0.72) that were identical to those reported by Newman et al. (2010). Only the RMSEA values differed slightly where our analysis yielded a value 0.006 lower than the value of 0.180 reported by Newman.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Therefore, interpretation of relationships between factors such as those made by Newman et al. (2010) –and others –require analyses similar to those reported in the present study.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original meta-analytic data reanalysed with variance decomposition, challenging redundancy interpretation. Original 2010 numerical model explicitly recovered up to minor fit-index variation; numerical reproduction of 2011 is not separately established. Both publications are directly re-examined; 2010 supplied the data and original numerical model, while 2011 states the challenged claim. Partial full-text extraction limits certainty, especially the scope of the 2010 robustness verdict.

corrected_value.title: Job attitudes and employee engagement: Considering the "A-factor".
corrected_value.authors: Newman, D. A., Joseph, D. L., & Hulin, C. L.

prior_decision.quote: Analyses not conducted in Newman et al. (2010) (Handbook of Employee Engagement: Perspectives, Issues, Research, and Practice, pp. 43–61) were performed to deconstruct the explained variance in work engagement into commonality coefficients representing all possible subsets of variables.
prior_decision.reason: Newman et al. (2010) is an omitted reproduction target: the authors explicitly re-estimated its structural equation model (Figure 4.3, Panel A) on its meta-analytic correlation matrix, recovering identical latent correlations, and then decomposed the model's variance to challenge its substantive conclusions regarding construct redundancy.

shipped_originals.title_o: Special education services provided to students with and without parental reports of traumatic brain injury

blind_target.evidence_quote: The purpose of this study is to replicate a study conducted by Hux, Marquardt, Skinner, and Bond (1999) in which the researchers explored the frequency of traumatic brain injuries (TBI) in the special education population as compared to the frequency of TBI among students in general education.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Results indicated that the sample in the current study reported a lower incidence rate of TBI than the general population as well as that in the 1999 study by Hux and colleagues. Additionally, only one student in the current sample (5% of TBI group) reported a history of TBI along with receiving special education services. Discrepancies between the current study and the Hux and colleagues (1999) study are explored, and possible reasons for the discrepancies are discussed.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit discrepancies from original incidence and special-education findings. Full reference unavailable.
